title: Exploring Inflammatory-related Hub Genes as Therapeutic Targets in Major Depressive Disorder: Implications for Immunological Pathways.
authors: Wang, Ruiqi; Fan, Hongyuan; Feng, Yu; Li, Haibo; Cui, Jin
journal: Iranian journal of allergy, asthma, and immunology
one_liner_zh: 该研究聚焦抑郁症炎症相关枢纽基因的免疫通路分析，仅涉及转录因子调控网络构建，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: This study explored the mechanisms of action of inflammation related central genes in severe depression (MDD) and analyzes their potential as therapeutic targets. By identifying key genes and establishing the link between immune regulatory mechanisms and depression, we provide a theoretical basis for developing more accurate diagnostic and treatment methods. Gene expression datasets related to MDD were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) associated with inflammatory processes were identified and analyzed through Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed to identify hub genes. Additionally, we explored regulatory networks of miRNAs, transcription factors, and potential drug interactions were explored. Immune infiltration analysis was performed to examine immune cell profiles. Seven key genes-HMGB1, HSP90AB1, MAPK1, MMP9, MYD88, S100A12, and TLR2-were identified as central players in the inflammatory pathways underlying MDD. These genes demonstrated moderate diagnostic accuracy with AUC values ranging from 0.5 to 0.7. Enrichment analyses revealed significant associations with immune signaling pathways, including IL-17 and Toll-like receptor signaling. Immune infiltration analysis highlighted altered abundances of regulatory T cells, neutrophils, and dendritic cells in MDD samples. Inflammatory-related hub genes play crucial roles in linking immune dysregulation to the pathophysiology MDD pathophysiology. These findings offer insights into the immunological underpinnings of MDD and present potential therapeutic targets for intervention through immune-modulatory approaches.
abstract_zh: 本研究探讨了严重抑郁症（MDD）中炎症相关中枢基因的作用机制，并分析了其作为治疗靶点的潜力。通过识别关键基因并建立免疫调节机制与抑郁症之间的联系，我们为开发更精确的诊断和治疗方法提供了理论基础。从基因表达综合数据库（GEO）获取了与MDD相关的基因表达数据集。鉴定了与炎症过程相关的差异表达基因（DEGs），并通过基因本体论（GO）和京都基因与基因组百科全书（KEGG）富集分析进行了分析。构建了蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络以识别枢纽基因。此外，我们探索了miRNAs、转录因子的调控网络以及潜在药物相互作用。进行了免疫浸润分析以检查免疫细胞谱。七个关键基因——HMGB1、HSP90AB1、MAPK1、MMP9、MYD88、S100A12和TLR2——被确定为MDD炎症通路中的核心参与者。这些基因显示出中等诊断准确性，AUC值范围为0.5至0.7。富集分析揭示了与免疫信号通路（包括IL-17和Toll样受体信号）的显著关联。免疫浸润分析强调了MDD样本中调节性T细胞、中性粒细胞和树突状细胞丰度的改变。炎症相关枢纽基因在连接免疫失调与MDD病理生理学中发挥关键作用。这些发现为MDD的免疫学基础提供了见解，并提出了通过免疫调节方法进行干预的潜在治疗靶点。
